metaTitle: Pest Control SEO Company: Maps, Pages and Pricing
metaDescription: Pest control SEO from ASP: service pages, Business Profile work and technical fixes, measured against booked jobs. No link buying. See what drives the cost.
intro: Pest control SEO is the work of showing up when someone near you searches for termite, rodent or mosquito help, in the map pack and the organic results. ASP builds the pages, Business Profile and technical health behind that, and reports it against booked jobs.

sections.heading: What pest control SEO covers
paragraphs: Pest control SEO has two halves. The map pack and your Google Business Profile decide who shows up for searches near the customer. The organic results and your service pages decide who looks credible enough to call.

On the map side, Business Profile data, review volume and recency, and citation consistency carry real weight. Local SEO Pro handles that work: profile management, citation audits across 60+ directories and a ranking heatmap from 50+ grid points a month. This page covers the organic side, and both land in one report.

sections.heading: Service pages for each pest you treat
paragraphs: Under the NAICS code for this trade, pest control covers birds, mosquitoes, rodents, termites and other insects and pests, and fumigation counts too. Each of those is its own search, with its own buyer and its own ticket size, so each one is planned on its own.

We build pages in order of what a booked job is worth to you, not by search volume alone. A strong service page grows into a cluster: the main page plus a cost breakdown, a treatment comparison and the seasonal problem, all linked together.
A service nobody searches for by name gets folded into a broader page. You see the page list before anything gets written.

sections.heading: Seasonal content that goes up before the rush
paragraphs: Some pest problems follow the calendar. CDC data puts peak tick activity in the warmer months, April through September, though exposure can happen year-round, so tick content needs to be live and indexed before April.

New problems show up too. BLS expects the growing number of invasive insect species to create demand for pest control services. When a new pest starts appearing in your area, a clear page on what it is and how you treat it gives local searchers a straight answer from a local company.

sections.heading: Putting your licenses and credentials on the page
paragraphs: According to BLS, most states require pest control workers to be licensed, usually after training and an exam. Federal law also requires anyone who applies or supervises the use of restricted use pesticides to be certified, and many state agencies require certification for all commercial pesticide use.

EPA tells homeowners shopping for termite work to ask to see the company's state license. We put license numbers, certifications and named, credentialed authors where buyers and search engines can find them. EPA's 2017 certification rule sets a maximum five-year recertification interval for commercial applicators, so the credentials on your site need a review date too.

sections.heading: Technical fixes and honest reporting
paragraphs: Before new pages go up, we fix what stops Google from reading the site: status codes, redirect chains, canonicals, schema, the sitemap and mobile load speed. Problems get fixed in order of what they cost you, not by an audit tool's severity score.

We don't buy links or sell link packages. Reports show rankings and impressions as early signs, then leads and booked jobs. Domain Authority is not in the report, because it is a third-party score Google does not use.

sections.heading: What pest control SEO costs
paragraphs: The price depends on your market and your site. The main drivers are the size of your market, how wide your service area is, how many services and locations need pages, and how much technical debt sits in the way. The audit sets the scope, and you see the number before you commit.
Organic SEO is not sold off a rate card here. It is scoped inside the tiers below after the audit, and current details are on our pricing page.

Foundation: $2,500 a month, which includes Local SEO Pro, the Content Creation Package and Housecall Pro attribution setup.

faqs.question: How long does pest control SEO take to work?
faqs.answer: There is no honest fixed timeline. It depends on your domain's history, the technical debt in the way and how competitive your market is. Technical fixes usually show first, on-page work next, and new content clusters move slowest but last longest.

faqs.question: Do you build backlinks for pest control websites?
faqs.answer: No. ASP does not buy links or sell link packages. Links that come from useful content, real partnerships and press coverage are worth having, and those are earned rather than bought.

faqs.question: Does every pest need its own page?
faqs.answer: Not always. We look at how often buyers search for it, what a booked job is worth and what the ranking pages already cover. A pest with steady searches and good margin gets built first; one nobody searches for by name is handled inside a broader page.

faqs.question: How is SEO different from Local Services Ads?
faqs.answer: Local Services Ads are a paid slot charged per lead, and you are visible while you pay. SEO is the organic and map work underneath, slower to build and still in place when ad spend pauses. Our pest control advertising page covers the paid side.

faqs.question: What does pest control SEO cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on market size, service area, the number of services and locations, and technical debt. Local SEO Pro is $1,200 a month, and the full tiers start at $2,500 a month. See the pricing page for current options.

faqs.question: How do you measure whether pest control SEO is working?
faqs.answer: Rankings and impressions show whether visibility is moving. Calls and form leads show whether it is landing, and booked jobs show whether it paid. Where your CRM supports it, we carry lead source through to the job.
